payload.root_cause: In `Inventory.reserve` (pyshop/inventory.py:20) the stock check uses a strict comparison `if self.available(sku) > qty:`. When a customer requests exactly the remaining available quantity (available == qty), the condition is False, control falls into the `else` branch and line 23 raises OutOfStock. This is an off-by-one boundary error: the condition must accept `available >= qty` (i.e., reject only when `available < qty`), matching the method's own docstring ('Reserving exactly the remaining quantity is allowed', line 17) and the documented domain rule in README.md ('Reserving exactly the remaining stock is allowed.'). The crash site (line 23) is merely the symptom; the defect is the operator on line 20.
evidence: pyshop/inventory.py:20 - `if self.available(sku) > qty:` uses strict `>`, excluding the case available == qty from the success path.

pyshop/inventory.py:23 - `raise OutOfStock(f"{sku}: requested {qty}, available {self.available(sku)}")` is reached for available == qty (3 == 3), matching the reported exception 'A: requested 3, available 3'.
pyshop/inventory.py:17 - docstring explicitly states 'Reserving exactly the remaining quantity is allowed', contradicting the implementation.

pyshop/inventory.py:13-14 - `available()` computes stock minus reserved; for Inventory({'A': 3}) with nothing reserved it returns 3, so the comparison 3 > 3 is False and the exact-quantity reserve fails.
tests/test_inventory.py:12-15 - failing test reserves 3 of 3 and expects available == 0 afterwards.

tests/test_inventory.py:6-9 and tests/test_inventory.py:18-21 - other reserve tests (2 of 5 succeeds, 2 of 1 raises) are consistent with the intended `>=` semantics, confirming only the boundary case is broken.
pyshop/cart.py:36 - the only other caller, `self.inventory.reserve(product.sku, qty)`, simply delegates to `Inventory.reserve`; there is no duplicate reservation logic to blame.
README.md domain rules - 'Reserving exactly the remaining stock is allowed.'
